correctness.rationale: Exact domain: all 28 nonline triples of the seven-point Fano plane, adjacent precisely on disjointness; every perfect matching has 14 edges. The graph has 42 edges and verified girth 7. A branch-on-uncovered-vertex recursion enumerates all 84 matchings, without omissions. For every unordered pair, the first checker forms the symmetric difference and counts 8-/10-length single alternating cycles; independent second checker generates matching-alternating cycles directly in the isomorphic seven-claw/ring graph. Both return 42 eight-switch edges (42 K2 components), 168 ten-switch edges (4-regular connected), identical distance layers (1,4,12,25,28,13,1) for each of 84 starts, unique antipodes at distance 6, exactly 42 pairs with difference cycle partition (8,16) and the converse, and eight-switch partners at ten-switch distance 5. The isomorphism permutation is explicitly checked. Crucially, the antipodal difference is TWO cycles of lengths 8 and 16, not a 24-cycle. Standalone certificates and recorded outputs are replayed from package paths.

Four-cycle hardness/structure is inapplicable in this girth-seven host.

value.rationale: The Coxeter graph is a canonical highly symmetric non-Hamiltonian cubic graph of girth seven. Fixed-length alternating-cycle switches form a natural perfect-matching reconfiguration model directly studied in the literature. The theorem determines a sharp transition from 42 isolated exchange pairs at cycle length eight to a connected four-regular state graph at length ten, and completely fixes its global radius, diameter and distance distribution. Its uniform unique antipode and exact disjoint 8+16 cycle characterization are structurally motivated, not arbitrary numeric slices. The invariant is not implied by the old one-factor count or unrestricted reachability and provides a precise benchmark for constrained matching dynamics.
